question:
A photoelectric experiment is performed using a clean metal cathode of work function $\phi=2.0\,\text{eV}$. The cathode is illuminated normally by monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda=400\,\text{nm}$.

The light beam is uniform and completely covers an active cathode area $A=4.0\,\text{mm}^2$. The intensity of light incident on the cathode is $I_1=62\,\text{W/m}^2$.

The anode is kept sufficiently positive so that the detector operates under saturation conditions (i.e., all emitted photoelectrons are collected). The measured saturation photocurrent is $I_{s1}=8.0\,\mu\text{A}$.

Define the quantum efficiency $\eta$ as
$$\eta=\frac{\text{number of collected photoelectrons per second}}{\text{number of incident photons per second}}.$$
Assume $\eta$ remains constant for this wavelength and in the given intensity range.

If the intensity is increased to $I_2=155\,\text{W/m}^2$ (same $\lambda$ and same $A$),

 Determine:

(i) the quantum efficiency $\eta$,

(ii) the new saturation photocurrent $I_{s2}$,

(iii) the stopping potential $V_s$ and whether it changes with intensity.

Use $hc=1240\,\text{eV}\cdot\text{nm}$ and $e=1.60\times10^{-19}\,\text{C}$.
